title: perf-canary: add cache-heavy prefix reuse scenario + KV cache regression gates
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes: Adds a new cache-heavy canary workload and gating thresholds for KV/prefix cache stability on the runtime release train; failures now block promotion unless waived by Runtime oncall.
description: Context: As part of the cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint (ENG-4819), we need a perf-canary workload that is explicitly cache-sensitive so we can (a) detect regressions in cache hit-rate / saved-prefill behavior and (b) catch runtime changes that preserve raw latency on average while silently degrading cache effectiveness (which shows up as cost + tail latency for real workloads). This PR adds a new scenario and wires it into the runtime release train gating. What’s included: 1) New scenario `kv_cache_prefix_reuse_heavy` that generates a high prefix-reuse distribution across N tenants/routes while keeping decode lengths realistic; the generator intentionally includes a small % of "prefix churn" to ensure we’re not masking lookup/evict regressions. 2) New metrics extracted from canary run artifacts: `cache_hit_rate`, `cache_hit_bytes_ratio`, `saved_prefill_ms_per_req`, and `cacheable_prompt_ratio` (when available); we treat missing telemetry as a soft-fail for now (warn) but require it for v2-enabled lanes. 3) Regression thresholds + gating policy: - For `kv_cache_prefix_reuse_heavy`: `cache_hit_rate` must not drop > 4.0 percentage points vs baseline, `saved_prefill_ms_per_req` must not drop > 8%, and `p95_prefill_ms` must not increase > 6% (all over 3-run median). - Adds noise control: gating triggers only if regression repeats in 2 consecutive runs OR exceeds a hard threshold (2x). - Adds a manual override mechanism via `CANARY_GATING_WAIVER=RUNTIME_ONCALL:<reason>` that logs to the summary artifact. 4) Integration with release gating for the runtime train: updates the release workflow to include the new scenario in `runtime-main` gates; Dedicated/Private lanes run it nightly only (to reduce GPU spend) until cache telemetry v2 is fully rolled out. 5) Docs: local run instructions + how to read the new cache metrics panels in the canary HTML report. Notes/assumptions: - This scenario is designed to be stable across GPU types; we normalize to per-request metrics and compare medians, but we still keep separate baselines per SKU family. - The cache metrics depend on the runtime exporting v2 telemetry fields; we degrade gracefully (warn-only) when those fields aren’t present, but gating is strict in the v2 lane. - This PR does not change any runtime code; it only consumes telemetry emitted by runtime builds. Testing: - Ran the scenario locally against runtime build `runtime@8c1d8c4` with `--repeat 5` and confirmed hit-rate stability within ~1.2pp run-to-run. - Verified gating logic by injecting a synthetic 10pp hit-rate drop in fixtures; gate blocks as expected and provides a clear diff in the report. Follow-ups: - Once v2 cache telemetry is fully enabled, switch missing-telemetry from warn -> fail across all lanes (tracked in ENG-4820). - Consider adding an additional "routing fragmentation" scenario once the attribution tags are fully stable (Logan/Nadia).
commits: canary/metrics: parse cache_hit_rate + saved_prefill_ms from run artifacts
gating: add threshold config + consecutive-regression detection
ci: wire scenario into runtime release train workflow
docs: local run + interpreting cache-heavy report sections
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed: Thresholds look reasonable, but I’m worried `saved_prefill_ms_per_req` will be noisy if partial-prefill classification changes. Can we gate primarily on hit-rate + prefill p95 and keep saved-prefill as an informative metric? Marcus Reed: Agreed on noise risk. I changed the policy so saved-prefill is gated only when the metric is present AND stable (we require coefficient-of-variation < 0.15 across repeats); otherwise it’s reported but not gating. Logan Wright: Can we please ensure missing telemetry is not silently ignored? We need to know when a runtime build stopped emitting cache fields. Marcus Reed: Added a "telemetry completeness" section in the report + a warning summary line in the GitHub check output. In the v2 lane, missing telemetry fails the gate; in non-v2 lanes it warns. Sergio Costa: Suggest adding an explicit hard threshold for hit-rate (e.g., absolute < 0.35) to catch baseline drift issues. Marcus Reed: Added `min_absolute_cache_hit_rate` for this scenario with SKU-specific baselines (0.38 for L4, 0.42 for H100). Allison Grant: Please document the waiver usage and require a reason string. Marcus Reed: Done; waiver requires `RUNTIME_ONCALL:<ticket-or-reason>` and is included in the artifacts + check output. Omar El-Sayed: One more thing—does the generator include multi-tenant tags? We’ve seen caching regress when routing splits traffic across routes. Marcus Reed: Yes; scenario supports `--routes 8 --tenants 20` with controlled skew. I set default to 4 routes / 10 tenants; can scale for nightly. Omar El-Sayed: LGTM after the saved-prefill gating tweak. Logan Wright: Approved. Sergio Costa: Approved. Allison Grant: Approved.
notes: Initial CI run failed due to ruff complaining about unused import in `cache_telemetry.py`; fixed in follow-up commit and re-ran checks. GPU smoke was re-run once after transient runner preemption.
